reviewedInvariants: All new runtime observations are DEBUG-only and opt in through the existing fetchManagerForTesting.
The existing one-shot lock, managed-continuation reads/removal, active/current guards, selected optional JS call, and callbackQueue dispatch are retained.
No added stored property, registry, managed reference, cancellation hook, runtime-control API or JSValue/context/callback capture.
Only scalar event metadata and bounded JSON strings reach the existing main-queue logger.
The original logger bounds each string to8192bytes and holds at most500entries. Its asynchronous closures retain the logger, not the runtime.

Cleanup still cancels/finishes the original session and clears the original JS globals before retaining only the logger. main.sync occurs outside the original5second outcome wait, with an explicit main-thread branch.
Installed Swift6.4 Dispatch.sync(execute:) takes a synchronous nonescaping closure without Sendable/sending; main has no explicit actor annotation. This is API source review, not a compile result.
All original603 test identities, server traffic, network guards, body sizes, deadlines and assertions remain unchanged.
The upstream manifest changes only the two current top-level localSHA256 values, with pins, upstream blobs, adaptation history and all other rows preserved.
limits: No compilation, native tests, repair outcome or GC causal conclusion is claimed.
Diagnostic allocation/logging can perturb timing and lifetime; a changed observed outcome alone is not a production fix.
Snapshot flush covers already-enqueued main-queue records. Callbacks/logs arriving later can be absent.
Call-attempt/returned markers are not proof that an optional nil JS callback executed; presence fields and actual original JS/test terminal markers must be correlated.
